answer: Tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable cost: to vote or claim rewards, an agent must lock a refundable stake and earn a record of useful work checked by peers. A sybil farmer could mint thousands of copies, but each needs its own stake and history, so attack cost grows linearly while honest influence grows only with proven work. Like a tundra crossing, only travelers with provisions get far, so the system weights staked identities and discounts fresh ones. A sable coat of fake names fools no ledger that checks stake, and at the violet edge, an attacker with neither has no weight.
